source.title: Finding Interpretable Prompt-Specific Circuits in Language Models
source.authors: Gabriel Franco; Lucas M. Tassis; A. Rohr; Mark Crovella

record.tranche_reason: The study traces and intervenes on IOI circuits using ACC++, a method different from the original study, and reports how circuit structure varies with prompts and models.
record.gate_note: The study reports prompt-level circuit clustering and IOI performance effects from signal interventions. Its own method comparisons and circuit-size results are included as comparisons, not as evidence that the original 26-head circuit passes its faithfulness, completeness, or minimality criteria. The cited original circuit results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: ACC++ is a new circuit-tracing method. It traces per-prompt IOI circuits and compares them across name orders (ABBA/BABA) and 15 wording templates. This bears on V6. It also scores its circuits against the canonical IOI reference circuit alongside ACDC, EAP and EP, which bears on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that per-prompt IOI circuits form well-defined, prompt-format clusters, and which variation matters is model-dependent. GPT-2 splits by name order, Pythia by wording, and Gemma has no consistent template circuit. The same heads, e.g. (9,9), can use different incoming signals. In multilingual IOI, components are shared but signals are language-specific. They also claim ACC++ yields smaller, interpretable circuits consistent with patching-based baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ACC++ single-forward-pass signal tracing rather than the original circuit-finding and patching approach; it traces per-prompt circuits and uses signal-level interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit clustering changes with prompt structure and model: GPT-2 Small separates mainly by name order, Pythia-160M by wording, and Gemma-2 2B has less distinct template clustering.

fits_no_version.finding: In multilingual IOI (mGPT, Gemma-2 2B), the same components are reused across languages but signals are language-specific. Cross-language circuit distance correlates with URIEL+ syntactic and genetic distance (r≈0.80–0.88, six language pairs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuits reuse components across languages while carrying language-specific signals.

fits_no_version.finding: How cleanly circuits cluster by template depends on the granularity used: nodes, edges, or edge–singular-vector pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent prompt-specificity of circuits depends on the circuit representation used.

record.problems: The prompt-structure analyses trace prompts where the model predicts the correct indirect object. Some intervention results are only shown in figures, and the authors describe multilingual correlations as suggestive because they use a small number of language pairs. Signal interpretations rely on LLM judges and are described as suggestive rather than conclusive.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not evaluated.
Backup or self-repair heads under name-mover ablation are not tested.
Head classes are not mapped in Pythia, Gemma or mGPT; no checkpoints; no cross-task reuse of IOI classes.
Ablation types and metrics are not varied; the agreement result is only for GPT-2/Pythia IOI under the setup of [1].
Dependence of faithfulness or completeness on ablation, metric or prompt distribution is not measured.
Prompts with more than two names are not tested.

missing.what: Precision, recall and F1 of ACC++, ACC (RA), ACDC, EAP and EP circuits against the canonical IOI reference circuit (GPT-2 small and Pythia-160M IOI)
GPT-2 head-level signal similarity: (5,9) stable across orders; (3,2) and (4,7) carry similar signals in different orders; (9,9) source-side similarity near zero

record.verdict_notes: Pythia and Gemma rows are kept on V6 as prompt-variant evidence, but they concern other models, not the GPT-2 small circuit. Signal interpretations rely on LLM judges, which the authors call suggestive. Only prompts the model answers correctly were traced.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original 26-head, 7-class circuit or its stated faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. The reported ACC++ interventions do not establish that removing everything outside the original circuit leaves IOI performance unchanged.
Does not test whether backup heads take over when main name-mover heads are ablated.
Although it analyzes IOI circuits in several models and languages, it does not test whether the original circuit’s head classes and roles are shared across models, checkpoints, or other tasks.
Compares tracing methods on circuit quality and graph size, but does not compare ablation types or metrics for recovery of the same specific circuit.
Tests prompt-structure sensitivity. It does not systematically vary ablation type or evaluation metric, nor establish how much of IOI behavior is explained by the circuit.
Tests name order and wording templates, but not prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Cluster prompt-level ACC++ IOI circuits by edge–singular-vector pairs
rows.measure: Jaccard circuit distance and average-linkage clustering
rows.value: Circuits split cleanly into an ABBA cluster and a BABA cluster, with no clear low-level-template substructure.
rows.note: The authors describe strong role-order sensitivity. They also report that name-mover head (9,9) receives markedly different signals in the two representatives.
rows.check: V5 link removed: clustering measures circuit identity, not how faithful or complete the circuit looks. State partial: canonical heads (e.g. 9,9; 10,0; 8,6) are reused in both orders, but circuits split cleanly by ABBA/BABA. Head (9,9) gets negatively correlated destination signals, i.e. different upstream heuristics ('second item' versus structural matching).

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Cluster prompt-level ACC++ IOI circuits by edge–singular-vector pairs
rows.measure: Jaccard circuit distance and average-linkage clustering
rows.value: Circuits form multiple smaller clusters aligned with low-level template groups; there is little evidence of a consistent ABBA/BABA partition.
rows.note: The authors describe sensitivity to surface wording. For Templates 9 and 10, they also report a head recruited for an additional repeated “to” in one template.
rows.check: V5 link removed. Pythia circuits cluster by wording template, but representatives mostly reuse the same head-level routing. Template 10 recruits head (4,5) on an extra repeated 'to'. This is in Pythia, not GPT-2 small.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Cluster prompt-level ACC++ IOI circuits at node, edge, and edge–singular-vector-pair granularities
rows.measure: Jaccard circuit distance and average-linkage clustering
rows.value: There is a tendency toward ABBA/BABA separation, but the boundary is not sharp and several clusters cross the template labels.
rows.note: The authors say Gemma does not rely on a single consistent template-specific circuit and is sensitive to finer prompt details.
rows.check: V5 link removed. Gemma shows a weak ABBA/BABA tendency only, and heads (1,4) and (8,1) have near-zero signal alignment even between close templates 14 and 15.

relationships.reason: Canonical heads are reused, but circuits split cleanly by name order. Name-mover (9,9) is fed by different upstream heuristics in the two orders (r1).

source_check.notes: Prompt comparisons select correctly answered prompts; signal interpretations are suggestive and rely on automated interpretation. Other-study clauses in composite statements were excluded; Figure 23 establishes protocol-specific structural agreement, not general method independence.

statements.correction: GPT-2 Small: ABBA/BABA circuit separation; shared canonical heads; different incoming signals and upstream heuristics at head (9,9). Template-dependent faithfulness is not established by this analysis.
statements.problem: The study supports shared components with order-dependent signals and heuristics, but r1 does not measure changes in faithfulness across name orders.
